standard.title: Elements of drama in improvisation
standard.description: use the elements of drama to explore and develop ideas for dramatic action in improvisations and/or devised drama
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use elements of drama — role, place, situation, language, movement — in dramatic play and process drama (Y1-2). They can identify and use drama vocabulary and take on roles purposefully.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use the elements of drama to explore and develop ideas for dramatic action in improvisations and/or devised drama.

nodes.label: Experimenting with voice as a dramatic tool
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can experiment with vocal qualities — loudness, pace, pitch — to create and differentiate roles, situations and atmosphere.
nodes.minimum_width: Student makes at least one deliberate vocal choice (e.g. changes pace or pitch) to signal a character, situation, or emotional state.
nodes.typical_width: Students experiment with loudness/softness, pace and pitch of their voices when initiating and developing roles and situations; they explore how voice choices create time, place and character; they use language choices (word selection, tone) to heighten tension.
wider: Students compare how the same line of dialogue produces different dramatic effects when delivered with different vocal qualities
Students explore non-vocal sound (clapping, rhythmic patterns) as a transition tool between scenes
nodes.hinge_reason: Voice is a primary expressive tool in drama; students who default to a single register cannot effectively create distinct roles or atmospheres, limiting their ability to shape dramatic action in the devising strand.

response_modes.reason: Vocal range develops through repeated guided practice — regular vocal warm-ups and focused short exercises where students try multiple voice qualities for the same role or situation.

success_criteria: Student makes at least one deliberate vocal choice (pace, pitch, or loudness) to create a character or atmosphere
Student can describe what their vocal choice was communicating

nodes.label: Using movement and space in dramatic action
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use movement, stillness and spatial awareness to develop dramatic action and manipulate tension.
nodes.minimum_width: Student makes at least one spatial or movement choice (proximity, stillness, gesture) that contributes to the dramatic meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Students develop spatial awareness — considering how close/far apart they stand and how movement manipulates tension; they use facial expressions and movement to sustain role; they improvise ways to connect short scenes through movement or rhythmic transitions.
wider: Students experiment systematically with how proximity between characters communicates relationship and power
Students explore how stillness and silence function as dramatic elements, not simply as pauses

response_modes.reason: Build a movement vocabulary through structured exercises: exploring proximity, levels, tempo, stillness — students need a toolkit of spatial choices before they can select intentionally.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The interplay of voice, movement and space in creating dramatic meaning is rich; students who experiment widely with spatial and physical drama tools develop stronger expressive range across all Drama strands.
success_criteria: Student uses at least one spatial or movement choice that contributes to dramatic meaning
Student can explain what their movement choice was communicating in the drama

nodes.label: Combining elements to develop dramatic action
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can combine elements of drama — voice, movement, language, space — to explore and develop ideas for dramatic action.
nodes.minimum_width: Student uses at least two elements in combination when developing a dramatic action sequence.
nodes.typical_width: Students combine voice, movement, language and space to develop roles, situations and tension; they use improvisation to generate ideas for devised drama; they explore how manipulating specific elements creates different effects and meanings.
wider: Students explore how language choice and movement combine to communicate status and power relationships in drama
Students use a specific element (e.g. silence, proximity) as a structural device to shape a complete improvised scene

response_modes.reason: Combining elements into coherent dramatic action is the integration move here; support students to reflect ('Which elements are you using? Is the effect what you intended?') after each improvisation.

success_criteria: Student combines at least two elements of drama in a sustained improvisation or devised sequence
Student identifies at least two element choices they made and describes their effect on the drama
